title: DISCOVERING YOUR NEW SELF: PART I

blocks.text: Introduction: Before Saul had his first encounter with God on the way to Damascus, he was an avowed enemy of the Lord Jesus Christ. But after the experience on the way to Damascus, he became a different person. He was commissioned and he started preaching the same gospel he had prosecuted. {{act 9:1,act 9:2,act 9:3,act 9:4,act 9:5,act 9:6,act 9:7,act 9:8,act 9:9,act 9:10,act 9:11,act 9:12,act 9:13,act 9:14,act 9:15,act 9:16,act 9:17,act 9:18,act 9:19,act 9:20,act 9:21,act 9:22|Acts 9:1-22}} Saul (later Paul) was a servant or slave of the Law, culture and traditions but was turned to a s ervant of God in righteousness.

cards.heading: 1. Knowing who you were before salvation and now saved

blocks.text: a. You were a servant of sin, a child of the devil that now has been delivered from sin and its passions. {{rm 6:16,rm 6:17,rm 6:18,rm 6:19|Rom. 6:16-19}}; 7:5-6; {{jo 8:24,jo 8:44|Jn 8:24,44}}; I Jn3: 8 b. You who were being taken captive, afflicted and dehumanized at will by the devil, are now delivered totally from the power of darkness and translated into the kingdom of the Lord Jesus Christ. {{2tm 2:26|II Tim 2:26}}; {{lk 13:11,lk 13:12,lk 13:13,lk 13:14,lk 13:15,lk 13:16|Luke 13:11-16}}; {{cl 1:12,cl 1:13,cl 1:14|Col. 1:12-14}} c. You were once no people, alien to the commonwealth of Israel and strangers to the covenant of promise. Now you have been made Son, in fact joint heir with the Lord Jesus Christ and thereby made entitled to all divine blessings. Rom.9: 25-26 {{eph 2:11,eph 2:12,eph 2:13,eph 2:14,eph 2:15,eph 2:16,eph 2:17,eph 2:18,eph 2:19,eph 2:20,eph 2:21,eph 2:22|Eph. 2:11-22}}; {{rm 8:17|Rom. 8:17}}; {{eph 1:3|Eph. 1:3}}; {{2pe 1:3,2pe 1:4|II Peter 1:3-4}}; {{1pe 2:9,1pe 2:10|I Peter 2:9-10}} d. Satan rule and authority over you since you lost your first position due to sin. However, the new you is now restored back to that of the former position and you now bear rule, power, dominion and dominion and authority over Satan and his cohorts. {{2tm 2:25,2tm 2:26|II Tim 2:25-26}}; {{lk 4:6|Luke 4:6}}; {{cl 1:20,cl 1:21,cl 1:22|Col 1:20-22}}; {{lk 9:1|Luke 9:1}}; 10:17-20; {{jm 4:7|James 4:7}};

cards.heading: 2. How does God see you now?

blocks.text: a. A new person entirely whose sins have both been washed away and forgotten.{{2co 5:17|II Cor. 5:17}}; {{gl 6:15|Gal 6:15}}; {{hb 8:12|Heb. 8:12}}; {{re 1:5|Rev. 1:5}}; {{1jo 1:7|I John 1:7}}; {{1jo 1:7|I John 1:7}}; {{is 44:22|Isa. 44: 22}}; {{rm 8:1|Rom. 8:1}}; {{1jo 5:13|I John 5:13}}. Sins mentioned here include every manner of sin committed in the past. b. As being holy and peculiar to Him. He has consequently kept you as the apple of His eye. {{1pe 2:9|I Peter 2:9}}; {{tt 2:14,tt 2:15|Titus 2:14-15}}; {{ex 19:5,ex 19:6|Ex. 19:5-6}}; {{dt 32:10|Deut. 32:10}}; {{zc 2:8|Zech 2:8}}; {{is 54:15,is 54:16,is 54:17|Isa. 54:15-17}}

conclusion.text: Your position is exactly like that of Saul mentioned in the introduction. You (put your name) were weak before, but now made strong. You were an under-dog to Satan, but now his master. You are now to bind him and secure from his hands, those he is still holding captive.
